en: n. a person who works in politics, especially as an elected member of a government; a person who is skilled at gaining power by using political tricks
ex: The politician promised to lower taxes if he was elected.
那位政治人物承諾當選後會降低稅賦。

en: n. the activities of governments and of people who try to influence how a country is governed; a particular set of political beliefs; the study of government
ex: He decided to go into politics after he left the army.
他退伍後決定投身政界。

en: n. an act of voting; a survey of the opinions of a group of people; the number of votes recorded; vt. to ask people their opinion about something
ex: A recent poll shows that most people support the new law.
最近的民意調查顯示大多數人支持這項新法律。

en: n. the process of making air, water or soil dirty and harmful; harmful substances that make things dirty or unsafe
ex: Air pollution is a serious problem in many big cities.
空氣污染在許多大城市是個嚴重的問題。

en: n. a hard, shiny white material made by baking clay at a high temperature; objects such as cups, plates or ornaments made from this material
ex: The museum has a large collection of ancient porcelain.
這間博物館收藏了大量古代瓷器。

en: n. a painting, drawing or photograph of a person; a description of someone or something in words; a page layout that is taller than it is wide
ex: The artist painted a portrait of the old fisherman.
畫家為那位老漁夫畫了一幅肖像。

en: vt. to arrange for something to happen at a later time than planned; vi. to delay doing something
ex: The match was postponed because of heavy rain.
因為大雨，比賽延期了。

en: n. pots, dishes and other objects made from baked clay; the art or craft of making such objects; a place where such objects are made
ex: She took a pottery class to learn how to make bowls.
她去上陶藝課學做碗。

en: n. the state of being very poor; a lack of something important
ex: Millions of families still live in poverty around the world.
全世界仍有數百萬個家庭過著貧困的生活。

en: n. a dry substance made of very small particles; a substance like this used on the skin or in cooking; gunpowder; vt. to cover with powder; vi. to turn into powder
ex: She put some powder on her face before the party.
她在派對前往臉上撲了一些粉。

en: a. very valuable or important; greatly loved or cherished; (informal) too refined or affected in manner
ex: Time is precious, so let's not waste any of it.
時間很寶貴，所以別浪費任何一點。

en: n. the fact of being in a place; a person who is felt to be near, especially one that cannot be seen; a confident and impressive manner
ex: Your presence at the meeting is required.
你必須出席這場會議。
ph: 讓人感受到某人的存在

en: v. to behave as though something is true when you know it is not; to claim to have a particular quality or skill when you do not
ex: The children pretended to be pirates in the garden.
孩子們在花園裡假裝自己是海盜。

en: a. existing or happening before something else or before the time you are talking about; too hasty
ex: She has no previous experience in sales.
她以前沒有銷售方面的經驗。

en: n. a series of actions taken to achieve a result; a natural series of changes; vt. to deal with something in a set way; to treat food or materials in a factory; to bring formal legal action against someone
ex: The application process usually takes about two weeks.
申請流程通常需要大約兩週。

en: n. a person or company that makes goods or grows food; a person who is in charge of making a film, play or TV show
ex: The film producer visited the set every day.
電影製片每天都會到片場。

en: n. something that is made or grown to be sold; a result of an action or process; (math) the number obtained by multiplying two numbers
ex: The company will launch a new product next month.
公司下個月將推出一項新產品。

en: n. a teacher of the highest rank at a university
ex: The professor gave a lecture on ancient history.
教授發表了一場關於古代歷史的演講。

en: n. things that you own; land and buildings; a quality or feature of something
ex: The thieves stole a lot of valuable property from the house.
小偷從那棟房子偷走了許多貴重財物。

en: n. a machine that moves liquid or air; a device for putting air into something; vt. to move liquid or gas using a pump; to ask someone many questions in order to get information
ex: He used a pump to inflate the bicycle tire.
他用打氣筒替自行車輪胎打氣。

en: n. a hit with the fist; a tool for making holes in paper or metal; a drink made from fruit juice, spices and wine; vt. to hit someone with the fist; to make a hole in something
ex: He punched the wall in anger.
他憤怒地一拳打在牆上。

en: n. a small bag for carrying money, used mainly by women; money available for a purpose; v. to pull your lips together tightly
ex: She took some coins out of her purse.
她從錢包裡拿出幾枚硬幣。

en: n. a piece of old cloth used for cleaning; a small piece of cloth or paper; (plural) old, worn-out clothes; vt. to tease someone in a joking way; to make fun of someone
ex: He wiped the oil off his hands with an old rag.
他用一塊舊抹布擦掉手上的油。
ph: a red rag to a bull

en: n. a measure of how fast something happens or how often something occurs; the amount of money charged; a level or grade; vt. to judge the quality or value of something
ex: The unemployment rate fell to its lowest level in ten years.
失業率降到十年來的最低點。

en: n. a sharp tool with a blade used for removing hair from the face or body; vt. to cut hair with a razor
ex: He shaved off his beard with a razor.
他用刮鬍刀刮掉了鬍子。

en: vi. to behave or change in a particular way because of something that has happened; to be affected by a substance or action
ex: How did she react when she heard the news?
她聽到消息時有什麼反應？

en: n. what you do or say as a result of something that has happened; a change that is caused by a chemical process; a feeling or opinion about something
ex: His reaction to the news surprised everyone.
他對這個消息的反應讓每個人都很驚訝。

en: n. a piece of paper showing that goods or money have been received; the act of receiving something; vt. to write on a bill that payment has been received
ex: Please keep the receipt in case you want to return the item.
請保留收據，以備退貨之用。

en: vt. to know who someone is or what something is because you have seen or heard them before; to accept officially that something is true or important; to show appreciation of someone's work
ex: I didn't recognize you with your new hairstyle.
我沒認出你換了新髮型。

en: n. a flat shape with four straight sides and four right angles, where opposite sides are the same length
ex: Draw a rectangle that is five centimeters long and three wide.
畫一個長五公分、寬三公分的長方形。

en: vt. to make something smaller in size, amount or price; to bring someone or something to a worse state; vi. to become smaller; to lose weight
ex: We must reduce the amount of plastic we use.
我們必須減少塑膠的使用量。

en: a. relating to a particular area of a country or the world
ex: The regional manager visits each branch once a month.
區域經理每個月拜訪一次各分公司。

en: n. a feeling of sadness about something that you wish you had not done; vt. to feel sorry about something you have done or not done; vi. to feel sorry
ex: I regret not studying harder when I was young.
我後悔年輕時沒有更用功讀書。

en: vi. to become less tense and worried; to rest after work; vt. to make a muscle or part of the body less tight; to make a rule less strict
ex: I like to relax by listening to music after work.
我下班後喜歡聽音樂放鬆。

en: vt. to allow someone to leave a place where they were kept; to let something go; to make something available to the public; n. the act of freeing someone or something; a new product or announcement
ex: The singer will release a new album next week.
那位歌手下週將發行新專輯。

en: a. connected with religion; having strong belief in a religion; done very carefully and regularly; n. a monk or nun
ex: She comes from a deeply religious family.
她來自一個虔誠信教的家庭。

en: vi. to stay in the same place or condition; to continue to exist after others have gone; to be left after other things have been used or removed
ex: Please remain seated until the plane has landed.
請在飛機降落前繼續坐在座位上。

en: vt. to act or speak officially for someone; to be a sign or symbol of something; to describe or show something in a particular way; vi. to raise an objection
ex: Each country sent a delegate to represent its people.
每個國家都派出一名代表來代表人民。

en: n. a person who is chosen to speak or act for others; a member of a legislature; a typical example; a. typical of a group or type of thing
ex: She is the sales representative for our region.
她是我們區域的業務代表。

en: n. a country or system of government in which power is held by the people and their elected representatives, and which has a president rather than a king or queen
ex: The Republic of China was founded in 1912.
中華民國成立於一九一二年。
